passage: After the cartoon, an advert came on: a shiny robot flipped into a truck while kids cheered. Siddiq sat straight up on the sofa in the Cape Town flat. "I need that," he told his cousin Thabo. Thabo didn't look up from his snack. "You said that about the glow yo-yo." Siddiq went quiet. He thought of the yo-yo, dull now in the bottom drawer. He got a sticky note, wrote "Robot: ask again Saturday," and pressed it on the fridge. On Wednesday he noticed he'd stopped thinking about it. On Saturday he still liked the robot, but not in a burning, desperate way. He shrugged and went out to kick the ball with Thabo instead.

qa.q: What did the robot in the advert do?
What was Siddiq feeling when he said, "I need that"?
qa.a: He felt excited and full of longing after the advert; he sat straight up and spoke as if the robot could not wait.

qa.q: What small step helped Siddiq sort out his wanting?
qa.a: Writing a note to ask again on Saturday gave him time to see whether he still wanted the robot or had only been caught by the advert.

qa.q: How does Thabo see Siddiq's sudden wanting?
qa.a: He has seen it before with the glow yo-yo, so he reminds Siddiq gently and does not take it too seriously.

grounding: A child feels an instant need for an advertised toy and pauses to see whether the wanting lasts.
